concurrent case, all intersections collapse to a single point, drastically reducing the number of pieces added per new cut.","The general lines in a plane problem is not bounded by a closed shape like a pizza."],"overturn_conditions":["If it is shown that the 4th cut, by some geometric trick of finite thickness, can avoid the exact center or intersect multiple times, the maximum could be a region.","The k-th line adds a number of regions equal to the number of existing lines it crosses plus 1 (or 2 if circular).","Both rely on the combinatorial addition of regions as cuts/lines are constraint."]},"claim":"The maximum number of pieces produced by 4 straight cuts through the exact center is 8, because the constraint of concurrency prevents the fourth cut from adding more than 2 C(0)=1. The 1st cut adds 1 piece -> C(1)=2. Each subsequent cut (k \u2265 2) intersects the previous k-1 lines at the identical center point. It passes through 2 existing regions, split by that point, adding exactly 2 new pieces. Therefore C(n)=1+1+2(n-1)=2n, and for n=4, C(4)=8.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
